headline: 36 missing children's bodies recovered in 8 months; 155 killed in total
summary: Human rights organization Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK) reports a grim statistic of child deaths, highlighting a severe crisis in child safety across the nation.
details: According to human rights organization Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK), the bodies of 36 missing children were recovered in the first eight months of the year. This includes cases where children were found buried or in rivers after being reported missing.

Beyond missing children, ASK's data compiled from various media reports reveals a total of 155 child deaths from January to August. These deaths resulted from physical torture (68), family violence (49), rape-murder (26, including two boys), attempted rape-murder (4), gunshots (3), physical torture of domestic workers (2), harassment (2), and abduction-murder (1).

Recent incidents include a 13-year-old in Cumilla, a 7-year-old in Jamalpur found buried after rape and murder, and a 10-year-old in Pabna found in a ditch, also after alleged rape and murder. Two suspects were arrested in each of these cases.

Tragically, some children were killed alongside family members. In Lakshmipur, a mother and her three daughters (ages 10, 17, 21) were hacked to death. In Rangpur, a 12-year-old boy was killed with his retired teacher father, mother, and adult sister.

Another case in Madaripur saw a one-year-old's body recovered from a river five days after his mother's body was found. Police confirmed both were murdered. In Sunamganj, three siblings (ages 10, 7, 2) from the same family were killed overnight on September 18.

The police headquarters reported that 15,717 children went missing in the first seven months of the year. While 13,679 (over 87%) have been rescued, 2,038 children remain missing, accounting for approximately 13% of the total.

UNICEF expressed deep concern over child rape and murder in Bangladesh on May 22, calling for an end to impunity. The organization urged for child safety to be ensured in homes, institutions, and all societal spheres.

Professor Fatema Rezina Iqbal, Chairman of Dhaka University's Sociology Department, stated that such brutality against children is deeply alarming. She questioned where children can truly be safe, noting that playgrounds, friends' outings, or even family environments no longer guarantee their security.

Professor Iqbal suggested that distorted mentalities, revenge, or family disputes could be behind these crimes, with children often becoming victims of adult conflicts. She emphasized that swift and exemplary justice could raise public awareness and help reduce such offenses.

headline: Three arrested in Cumilla school student murder; victim's phone recovered
summary: Ishayat Shahriar Apratim, a Class 7 student and son of a Cumilla University professor, was found dead a day after he went missing. Police have detained three suspects in connection with the case.
details: Ishayat Shahriar Apratim, the only child of Nahida Begum, an Associate Professor of Bengali at Cumilla University, was found dead on Saturday. The Class 7 student of Cumilla Border Guard School had been missing since Friday afternoon.

Apratim left his home on Friday around 3:30 PM, telling his mother he was going to Shalban Bihar with friends to take photos using her iPhone. When he did not return by evening, his mother filed a general diary (GD) at Cumilla Sadar Dakshin Police Station.

His body was discovered on Saturday around 1 PM on a hill behind Magic Paradise Park, near Cumilla University. Following an autopsy at Cumilla Medical College morgue, his body was handed over to his family at 8 PM.

Police have detained three individuals based on CCTV footage as suspects in Apratim's murder. Initially, a young man named Tuhin was arrested, and information obtained from his interrogation led to the subsequent arrests of Fahim and Anas.

The first Janaza (funeral prayer) for Apratim was held on Sunday at 10 AM at Cumilla University grounds, his mother's workplace. A second Janaza followed at 11 AM in Dakshin Bagmara, Kotbari area, after which he was laid to rest.

A Class 7 student, Apratim, was found dead in Cumilla after going missing with his mother's iPhone. Police have arrested three suspects in connection with the murder.

His body was discovered on Saturday around 1 PM on a hill behind Magic Paradise Park, near Cumilla University. Following an autopsy at Cumilla Medical College morgue, his body was handed over to his family at 8 PM.

Police have detained three individuals based on CCTV footage as suspects in Apratim's murder. Initially, a young man named Tuhin was arrested, and information obtained from his interrogation led to the subsequent arrests of Fahim and Anas.

The first Janaza (funeral prayer) for Apratim was held on Sunday at 10 AM at Cumilla University grounds, his mother's workplace. A second Janaza followed at 11 AM in Dakshin Bagmara, Kotbari area, after which he was laid to rest.
